title: Species & areas II: tiger, elephant, lion, cheetah

questions.q:
With reference to the legal and institutional framework for tiger conservation, consider the following statements:
1. The National Tiger Conservation Authority and the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau became statutory bodies through the 2006 amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
2. The NTCA is chaired by the Union Environment Minister.
3. Project Tiger is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme of the Environment Ministry.
4. The All India Tiger Estimation is conducted every five years.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The Act also requires State Tiger Conservation Plans, and a Tiger Reserve has a Core or Critical Tiger Habitat of highest protection, a buffer for conservation with sustainable livelihoods, and corridors. The AITE is run every four years by the NTCA and the Wildlife Institute of India, not every five.
questions.s: SPP notes B (CA Jul 2026, Shankar pp. 16-20)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the All India Tiger Estimation (AITE) 2022:
1. The figure of 3,682 is the mean estimate, while the minimum number of tigers actually photographed was 3,167.
2. It was the first cycle to assess ungulate prey across the country.
3. It was carried out by the NTCA together with the Zoological Survey of India.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Sources differ on the headline: Shankar's January piece cites 3,167 (the minimum count) while its July feature gives 3,682 (the mean, about 70% of wild tigers), so both figures are valid for different measures. The survey covered over 6.41 lakh sq km in 20 States and the partner was the Wildlife Institute of India, not the ZSI.
questions.s: SPP notes B (CA Jan and Jul 2026, Shankar)

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Tiger-monitoring tool : Function
1. M-STrIPES : GPS- and remote-sensing-based monitoring of field patrols
2. CaTRAT : Identifies individual tigers from stripe patterns
3. ExtractCompare : Automatically classifies camera-trap images by species
4. CA|TS : Certification launched at the St Petersburg Tiger Summit of 2010
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only pair 1 is correct. CaTRAT (Camera Trap Data Repository and Analysis Tool) sorts camera-trap images by species; ExtractCompare is the one that matches stripe patterns. Conservation Assured Tiger Standards were launched at the 1st Asian Parks Congress in Japan in 2013, and 23 Indian reserves are accredited, whereas St Petersburg 2010 gave International Tiger Day and the Tx2 goal.
questions.s: SPP notes B (CA Jul 2026, Shankar pp. 16-20)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about international tiger initiatives:
1. Under the Tx2 goal, the 13 tiger-range countries pledged to double wild tigers by 2022.
2. The Global Tiger Forum, headquartered in New Delhi, is the only intergovernmental body devoted solely to tigers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. Tx2 came out of the St Petersburg Tiger Summit of November 2010, which also gave International Tiger Day (29 July); India was among the few countries to meet it. The World Bank's Global Tiger Recovery Program has run since 2010, with GTRP 2.0 covering 2023-2034 through the Global Tiger Forum.
questions.s: SPP notes B (CA Jul 2026, Shankar pp. 16-20)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the reintroduction of tigers in Buxa Tiger Reserve:
1. Buxa lies in Assam, close to Kaziranga.
2. The first tigress, T138, was brought from the Sundarbans.
3. The reintroduction in Satkosia (Odisha) was held up as a success to emulate.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. Buxa is in Alipurduar, north West Bengal, bordering Bhutan's Phibsoo WLS, and links to Manas and Jaldapara. T138 came from Valmiki Tiger Reserve in the eastern Terai Arc, whose deciduous, riverine habitat matches Buxa, unlike the saline mangroves where Sundarbans tigers are adapted. Sariska and Panna (2008) succeeded; Satkosia failed for want of local consultation and because of conflict.
questions.s: SPP notes B (CA Wildlife Week 2026, Shankar pp. 97-98)

questions.q: In which pair of Tiger Reserves did tiger reintroduction succeed in 2008, offering the model that the NTCA now follows for sites such as Buxa?
questions.e: Sariska (Rajasthan) was repopulated from Ranthambore, using descendants of the tigress Machli, and is described as the world's first successful tiger translocation; Sariska now has about 53 tigers. Panna in Madhya Pradesh followed. Satkosia in Odisha is the cautionary failure; Buxa, Dampa and Palamau were listed for the Tiger Augmentation and Recovery Project.

questions.q:
With reference to elephant conservation in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Synchronous All India Population Estimation of Elephants (SAIEE) 2021-25 was India's first DNA-based synchronised elephant census.
2. SAIEE combined dung-DNA fingerprinting with block counts and line-transect surveys.
3. Gajah Suchana is the system that sends AI alerts to loco pilots about elephants on railway tracks.
4. The Captive Elephant (Transfer or Transport) Rules, 2024 were notified by the National Green Tribunal.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statements 1 and 2 are correct. SAIEE counted 22,446 wild elephants. Alerts to loco pilots come from Distributed Acoustic Sensing along tracks, with optical-fibre, seismic and thermal systems; Gajah Suchana is the national genetic database of captive elephants (DNA, morphology, ownership). The 2024 Rules follow a Supreme Court order of March 2023 and set up a High-Powered Committee for inter-State transfers.
questions.s: SPP notes B (CA Aug 2026, Shankar pp. 225-227)

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Elephant item : Detail
1. World Elephant Day : 12 September
2. Gajah Suchana : National genetic database of captive elephants
3. Typical elephant home range : About 10 to 30 sq km
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only one pair is correct. World Elephant Day is 12 August, and home ranges run from about 100 to 3,000 sq km, which is why corridors matter. India holds roughly 60% of the world's wild Asian elephants, with 33 Elephant Reserves, and train-hit deaths fell from 26 (2013) to 12 (2024). The sources give 150 corridors across 15 States in one place and 14 States in another.
questions.s: SPP notes B (CA Aug 2026, Shankar pp. 225-227)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Asiatic lion:
1. Its IUCN Red List status was lowered in risk from Critically Endangered to Endangered.
2. The mass lion deaths of 2018 were caused by Canine Distemper Virus.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. The 2018 outbreak, which killed over 20 lions, was caused by Canine Distemper Virus; babesiosis was linked to deaths in 2026, with possible CDV involvement. The official May 2025 census gives 891 lions (up from 674 in 2020), though the headline in one source says 'near 1,000', and the range now exceeds 35,000 sq km.
questions.s: SPP notes B (CA Aug 2026, Shankar pp. 230-231)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Asiatic lion's future:
1. Barda Wildlife Sanctuary has been developed as a second home for lions.
2. A Hi-Tech Monitoring Unit at Sasan Gir, set up in 2019, tracks lions through real-time radio telemetry.
3. A proposal to divert 75 ha of reserved forest for limestone mining threatens the Babarkot-Jafrabad corridor.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. Nearly half the lions already live outside strictly protected boundaries, so corridors link coastal groups to Gir; the mining proposal could cost about 5,000 mature trees and isolate satellite groups. With every wild lion in one Gir-centred landscape, the way ahead is a second secure population, disease management under Project Lion and maldhari-friendly compensation.
questions.s: SPP notes B (CA Aug 2026, Shankar pp. 230-231)

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the cheetah is correct?
o: Project Cheetah is implemented solely by the Wildlife Institute of India
The cheetah is the only large cat that can roar
The cheetah was declared extinct in India in 1972, the same year the Wildlife (Protection) Act was enacted
The African cheetah is IUCN Vulnerable, whereas the Asiatic cheetah is Critically Endangered
questions.e: The African cheetah is Vulnerable and the Asiatic cheetah, found in eastern Iran, is Critically Endangered. Cheetahs do not roar, unlike lions, tigers, leopards and jaguars. The cheetah was declared extinct in India in 1952. Project Cheetah (2022), implemented by the NTCA, was the world's first intercontinental translocation of a large wild carnivore.
questions.s: SPP notes B (CA Jan 2026, Vision IAS p. 85)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Project Cheetah:
1. The population stood at 50 as of December 2025, including 30 India-born cubs.
2. Nauradehi (Noradehi) was the first site beyond Kuno to receive cheetahs.
3. The two cheetahs brought from Botswana were released in Gandhisagar Wildlife Sanctuary.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. The population was 30 as of December 2025, including 19 India-born cubs. In the 2025 expansion phase, cheetahs went first to Gandhisagar Wildlife Sanctuary, with Noradehi and the Banni Grasslands planned next. The two Botswana cheetahs were released in Kuno National Park, Madhya Pradesh.
questions.s: SPP notes B (CA 2026, Shankar pp. 7-8; Vision IAS p. 85)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Landscape-level protection is needed for tigers, not just protection inside reserves.
Statement-II: According to the NTCA, 54% of tiger deaths in 2023 occurred outside tiger reserves.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I. With over half the deaths outside reserves, protecting only reserves misses most of the risk, hence the 2026 NTCA mortality database that records deaths inside and outside protected areas. Pressures include electrocution, poisoning, snaring, road and rail accidents, poaching and conflict. Madhya Pradesh, with 785 tigers in 2022, also recorded 45 deaths in 2026, about 40% of the national total.
questions.s: SPP notes B (CA Jul 2026, Shankar pp. 16-20)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Sariska's repopulation in 2008 is described as the world's first successful tiger translocation.
Statement-II: Ranthambore records cub survival of about 80%, among the best in India.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I. Sariska was repopulated with descendants of the Ranthambore tigress Machli (T-16, who bore 18 cubs), so the donor population mattered, but the cub-survival rate is a separate indicator of Ranthambore's quality. Rajasthan has 149 tigers, 72 in Ranthambore, and Sariska now has 53.
questions.s: SPP notes B (CA Jul 2026, Shankar pp. 16-20)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: India hosts about 70% of the world's wild tigers.
Statement-II: The All India Tiger Estimation is conducted every two years by the NTCA.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect. The AITE runs on a four-year cycle (the sixth cycle was under way in 2026), so a two-year gap is wrong. The tiger has been India's national animal since 1972 and the country has 58 tiger reserves in 18 States covering about 84,500 sq km (2.56% of the land).
questions.s: SPP notes B (CA Jul 2026, Shankar pp. 16-20)

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Asiatic lion is not correct?
o: Its range has expanded by over 16% to more than 35,000 sq km in Gujarat
The wild population is now spread evenly over two widely separated landscapes in different States
Nearly half of the population now lives outside strictly protected boundaries
Its IUCN status has improved from Critically Endangered to Endangered
questions.e: The last statement is wrong: all wild lions still live in one Gir-centred landscape in Gujarat, which is the single-population risk that Barda sanctuary is meant to ease. Gujarat's measures include Vanya Prani Mitras, machans for farmers, grassland restoration and railway speed limits and patrols.
questions.s: SPP notes B (CA Aug 2026, Shankar pp. 230-231)
